answer: Grant standing only for verifiable useful work: before an identity can vote or earn, it must finish public tasks whose output anyone can inspect — a knoll of small contributions piling into reputation. A sybil operator can script ten thousand accounts, but each one must actually do the work, so his bill is paid in real effort, not cheap registrations, and a raven-eyed audit of the ledger exposes copy-pasted output at once. Like a crystal, the record is transparent and hard to fake: identical submissions shatter together. The cost is peer review time, and newcomers start with no record.
